message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide for pulling *detailed* interface data on the most common platforms.  
Feel free to pick the section that matches your environment; I’ll also add a short Python snippet at the end so you can automate it if you prefer scripting over shell commands.

---

## 1️⃣ Linux / Unix‑like systems  

| Tool | What it shows | Typical usage |
|------|---------------|---------------|
| **`ip link show <iface>`** | Interface state, MAC, MTU, flags (UP/DOWN, PROMISC, etc.) | `ip link show eth0` |
| **`ip addr show <iface>`** | All addresses assigned to the interface (IPv4/IPv6, scope, prefix length) | `ip addr show eth0` |
| **`ip route show dev <iface>`** | Routes that use this interface | `ip route show dev eth0` |
| **`ethtool <iface>`** | Driver details, supported speeds, current negotiated speed & duplex, driver version, firmware | `sudo ethtool eth0` |
| **`ethtool -S <iface>`** | NIC statistics counters (rx/tx packets, errors, collisions, etc.) | `sudo ethtool -S eth0` |
| **`lspci -v -s $(lspci | grep Ethernet | awk '{print $1}')`** | PCI bus info + driver/module used | `lspci -v -s 02:00.0` |
| **`nmcli device show <iface>`** (NetworkManager) | Full NM report – all properties, connection profiles, DNS, routes | `nmcli device show eth0` |

### Example: Pull everything with one command

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
IFACE=${1:-eth0}

echo "=== Basic link info ==="
ip link show "$IFACE"

echo
echo "=== Address(es) ==="
ip addr show "$IFACE"

echo
echo "=== Route(s) via this iface ==="
ip route show dev "$IFACE"

echo
echo "=== Driver & hardware details ==="
sudo ethtool "$IFACE" | head -n 10   # first 10 lines for brevity

echo
echo "=== Statistics ==="
sudo ethtool -S "$IFACE" | head -n 20
```

Run it as root (`sudo ./show_iface.sh eth0`) to get the full output.

---

## 2️⃣ macOS  

| Command | What it shows | Usage |
|---------|---------------|-------|
| **`ifconfig <iface>`** | Flags, MAC, MTU, IPv4/IPv6, broadcast, netmask, etc. | `ifconfig en0` |
| **`networksetup -getinfo <device>`** | Current configuration (IP, subnet mask, router, DNS servers) | `networksetup -getinfo Wi-Fi` |
| **`networksetup -listallhardwareports`** | Maps device names to physical ports & MAC | `networksetup -listallhardwareports` |
| **`sysctl -a | grep -i <iface>`** | Kernel tunables related to the interface | `sysctl -a | grep -i en0` |

Example:

```bash
IFACE=en0
echo "=== ifconfig ==="
ifconfig "$IFACE"

echo
echo "=== NetworkSetup info ==="
networksetup -getinfo "$IFACE"
```

---

## 3️⃣ Windows (Command Prompt / PowerShell)

| Cmdlet / Tool | What it shows | Usage |
|--------------|---------------|-------|
| **`Get-NetAdapter -Name "<name>"`** (PowerShell) | Status, MAC, LinkSpeed, DriverVersion, MediaType | `Get-NetAdapter -Name "Ethernet"` |
| **`Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias "<alias>"`** | All IP addresses bound to the adapter | `Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias "Ethernet"` |
| **`Get-NetRoute -InterfaceAlias "<alias>"`** | Routing table entries for that adapter | `Get-NetRoute -InterfaceAlias "Ethernet"` |
| **`Get-NetTCPConnection -OwningProcess <pid> | Where-Object {$_.LocalAddress -eq "<ip>"}`** | Connections per process | `Get-NetTCPConnection -OwningProcess 1234` |
| **`wmic nic where Name="<name>" get /format:list`** | Raw WMI properties (speed, description, manufacturer, etc.) | `wmic nic where Name="Intel(R) Ethernet Connection" get /format:list` |

Example PowerShell script:

```powershell
$iface = "Ethernet"

Write-Host "=== Adapter basic info ==="
Get-NetAdapter -Name $iface | Format-List *

Write-Host "`n=== IP addresses ==="
Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias $iface | Format-Table IPAddress, PrefixLength, AddressFamily, Type

Write-Host "`n=== Routes ==="
Get-NetRoute -InterfaceAlias $iface | Format-Table DestinationPrefix, NextHop, RouteMetric, Protocol

Write-Host "`n=== WMI raw dump ==="
wmic nic where Name="$iface" get /format:list
```

---

## 4️⃣ Using SNMP (for remote devices)

If you have SNMP enabled on the target host, you can pull interface details programmatically:

```bash
snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifDescr
snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifPhysAddress
snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifOperStatus
snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifInOctets
```

Replace `public` with your community string and adjust OIDs for other metrics.

---

## 5️⃣ Quick Python helper (cross‑platform)

Using the `psutil` library you can fetch many of the same attributes without writing separate scripts for each OS.

```python
import psutil
import socket

def iface_details(iface):
    stats = psutil.net_if_stats().get(iface)
    addrs = psutil.net_if_addrs().get(iface)
    io_counters = psutil.net_io_counters(pernic=True).get(iface)

    print(f"--- {iface} ---")
    if stats:
        print(f"  IsUp: {stats.isup}")
        print(f"  Duplex: {stats.duplex}")
        print(f"  Speed(Mbps): {stats.speed}")
        print(f"  MTU: {stats.mtu}")

    if addrs:
        for addr in addrs:
            family = addr.family.name if hasattr(addr.family, 'name') else str(addr.family)
            print(f"  Addr Family: {family}")
            print(f"    Address: {addr.address}")
            if addr.netmask:
                print(f"    Netmask: {addr.netmask}")
            if addr.broadcast:
                print(f"    Broadcast: {addr.broadcast}")
            if addr.ptp:
                print(f"    PTP: {addr.ptp}")

    if io_counters:
        print("  IO Counters:")
        print(f"    Bytes Sent: {io_counters.bytes_sent}")
        print(f"    Bytes Received: {io_counters.bytes_recv}")
        print(f"    Packets Sent: {io_counters.packets_sent}")
        print(f"    Packets Received: {io_counters.packets_recv}")
        print(f"    Errors In: {io_counters.errin}")
        print(f"    Errors Out: {io_counters.errout}")
        print(f"    Drop In: {io_counters.dropin}")
        print(f"    Drop Out: {io_counters.dropout}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys
    iface_name = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None
    if not iface_name:
        print("Usage: python iface_info.py <interface>")
        sys.exit(1)
    iface_details(iface_name)
```

Install with `pip install psutil` and run: `python iface_info.py eth0`.

---

### TL;DR

| Platform | One‑liner for “full detail” |
|----------|-----------------------------|
| Linux | `ip -details link show eth0 && ip addr show eth0 && sudo ethtool -S eth0` |
| macOS | `ifconfig en0 && networksetup -getinfo Wi-Fi` |
| Windows PowerShell | `Get-NetAdapter -Name Ethernet | Format-List *; Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias Ethernet | Format-Table *` |
| Remote SNMP | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifDescr` |
| Cross‑platform script | `python iface_info.py eth0` (requires psutil) |

Pick the method that best fits your workflow—shell for quick manual checks, PowerShell for Windows admins, or the Python helper if you’re building a monitoring dashboard.
